questions.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & 6 \\ 2 & -2 & -5\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & -2 & -3 \\ -2 & 3-\lambda  & 6 \\ 2 & -2 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(A-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & -2 & -3 \\ -2 & 3-\lambda  & 6 \\ 2 & -2 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ -\lambda |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 6 \\ -2 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}|-(-2)|\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 \\ 2 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}|+(-3)|\begin{aligned}-2 & 3-\lambda  \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ -\lambda ({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda -3)+2(2\lambda -2)-3(2\lambda -2) & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+3\lambda )+(4\lambda -4)-(6\lambda -6) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+\lambda +2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 7 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $B$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\lambda =-5$ is an eigenvalue of $B$

II. $\lambda =-1$ is an eigenvalue of $B$

III. The eigenvalue $\lambda =-3$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-5-\lambda  & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 3-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 7 & -3-\lambda  & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(B-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4\times 4$ determinant across the $1$st column, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-5-\lambda  & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 3-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 7 & -3-\lambda  & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-5-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 7 & -3-\lambda  & 4 \\ 5 & 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3\times 3$ determinant across the $2$nd column, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-5-\lambda )\cdot (-3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & -2 \\ 5 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-5-\lambda )\cdot (-3-\lambda )((3-\lambda )(-1-\lambda )+10) & =0 \\ (\lambda +5)(\lambda +3)({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +7) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Since $D<0$ for the polynomial ${\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +7$, we have that the only real eigenvalues are $\lambda =-5$ and $\lambda =-3$ (both with algebraic multiplicity $1$).

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

questions.problem:
Determine all real eigenvalues $\lambda $ of the matrix 
$P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & -\lambda  & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is given by $det(P-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & -\lambda  & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 4 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}|+4|\begin{aligned}2 & -\lambda  \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}+6{\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda -12)-2(-2-2\lambda )+4(4+4\lambda ) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}+6{\lambda }^{2}+15\lambda +8 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}-6{\lambda }^{2}-15\lambda -8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to solve this equation. We find the first root by testing some values. According to the rational zeros theorem, a list of good first guesses consists of all divisors of $8:$ 

$$
\pm 1,\pm 2,\pm 4,\pm 8
$$

- Let's pick $x=1.$ Substituting to the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)^{3}-6(1)^{2}-15(1)-8 & =-28.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =1$ is not a root of the equation.

- Let's pick $x=-1.$ Substituting to the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)^{3}-6(-1)^{2}-15(-1)-8 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =-1$ is a root of the equation.

So, we can factor $(\lambda +1)$ out of ${\lambda }^{3}-6{\lambda }^{2}-15\lambda -8$ using synthetic division:

| $-1$ | $1$ | $-6$ | $-15$ | $-8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $↓$ | $-1$ | $7$ | $8$ |
|  | $1$ | $-7$ | $-8$ | $0$ |

So, we obtain the following factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\lambda +1)({\lambda }^{2}-7\lambda -8) & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)(\lambda +1)(\lambda -8) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=-1,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{2}=8.$

questions.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$R=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,R-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
R-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & -\lambda  & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(R-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st column, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(R-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & -\lambda  & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & 4 \\ 1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}|-(-2)|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda -4)+2(-2\lambda +7) & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}+4{\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -4)+(-4\lambda +14) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}+4{\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda +10 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}-4{\lambda }^{2}+3\lambda -10 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$P=[\begin{aligned}7 & 6 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & 6 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4-\lambda  & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 3-\lambda  & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(P-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Since the determinant of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix is given by the product of the entries on the main diagonal, we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & 6 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4-\lambda  & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 3-\lambda  & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )(-4-\lambda )(3-\lambda )(-5-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (\lambda -7)(\lambda +4)(\lambda -3)(\lambda +5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$
